sentence: This project studies children with severe aplastic anemia to compare treatments and find biomarkers that predict outcomes and complications.
This project tests a noninvasive technique that measures how severe ischemic heart disease is in patients.
This project studies why fibrin on implanted biomaterials makes macrophages fuse, and uses the findings to design biomaterials that reduce fusion.
This project studies how pathogenic T cells cause autoimmune disease in people with HLA-B27 syndromes and looks for ways to target them.
This project uses a sequencing technology to capture the expression profile of patients with frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project analyzes metabolites across many cancers to build a public resource that shows how tumor metabolism differs between tumors.
This project studies how genetic and epigenetic variability, aging and cancer cell metabolism affect tumor cells and cancer risk.
This project studies how specific enzymes in the protein degradation system help cells adapt to environmental challenges.
This project provides research services for studying dangerous pathogens safely, including tuberculosis, influenza and pathogens spread by vectors.
This project uses rabbits and mice to study how a virus stays latent, how tumor cells interact with bone, and a vaccine.
This project provides tools to measure metabolites and analyze molecular data, helping researchers study obesity and nutritional disorders.
This project tests heart muscle cells with gene variants to find which variants cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and why its severity varies.
This project studies how the immune system interacts with tumors and uses that knowledge to develop immunotherapies for cancer.
This project tests ways to make histotripsy safer and more precise for liver tumors in a large animal liver model.
This project studies how a transcription factor makes T cells exhausted and builds synthetic transcription factors to reprogram T cell function.
This project tries to find out what makes different regions of the skin differ from one another.
This project shares up-to-date information about hearing loss with professionals and families to support children learning to listen and speak.
This project studies how airway epithelial cells affect the aging immune system in the lung during viral infections.
This project tests whether gene expression scores can predict outcomes for patients with acute myeloid leukemia and studies the molecular basis of prognosis.
